gappers.catalyst: No ASTS-specific catalyst dated today; bounce after a -7.61% Nov 18 session blamed on launch-queue anxiety plus a rating downgrade, on top of a Nov 17 filing to issue 10M shares to Firefly Aerospace for a license/supply deal in which ASTS receives no cash.
headlines: Why Is AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) Stock Down -7.61% Today? (Tickeron, Nov 18)
AST Spacemobile files to offer 10M shares as part of Firefly agreement (Seeking Alpha, Nov 17)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No company news is dated Nov 19. The two live items are both from the prior two sessions. On Nov 17 ASTS filed to issue 10,000,000 shares to Firefly Aerospace under a license and supply agreement to develop a 20-ton rocket, receiving no cash in exchange -- straight dilution bought with equity. On Nov 18 the stock fell 7.61%, attributed to an accumulation of negatives rather than one headline: launch-queue anxiety, a published rating downgrade, and continued momentum deterioration. Standing fundamentals from Q3 2026 (Nov 9) are unchanged: 12 of ~45 planned satellites in orbit, commercial service not yet activated, ~$3.8B liquidity, $150-200M FY26 revenue guidance maintained. Shares sit ~79% below the $133.86 52-week high.
gappers.why: Mean reversion plus beta, not re-rating. ASTS is one of the highest-beta names in the space complex and fell hardest into yesterday's low, so a market-wide risk-on bounce lifts it most via short covering (~62M shares reported short) and dip-buying. The only dated company news -- a no-cash 10M-share issuance -- is dilutive and argues the other way.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day headline-free spike likely to mean-revert. 23.0M shares is real participation, but the move is explicitly complex-wide rather than idiosyncratic. Nothing fundamental improved: the durable milestone (commercial service activation) has slipped to YE26/early-2027, and yesterday's downgrade and launch-queue concern are unaddressed. The stock is simply recovering the ground it lost on Nov 18.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Driver is a market-wide bounce off an oversold extreme; the one dated company item is dilutive and the structural milestone slipped to 2027 -- no thesis trigger to carry past the session.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Book is flat ($100,000 equity, 0/6 positions, 0% deployed vs the 75-85% rule), so nothing is displaced; the cost is one of three weekly slots (0/3 used, week of Nov 16) spent on the weakest-evidence name on the list. Within today's list it is displaced by BE and KLIC, both of which carry dated company catalysts. R:R is the binding problem: buying into a +9.67% gap at $27.95 puts a rule-compliant stop (3% minimum distance, 7-10% band) at roughly $25.16-$26.00 -- i.e. at or below yesterday's $25.49 close -- so 2:1 needs about +15-19% ($32.1-$33.3) with no company catalyst to produce it. It also fails the Confluence rule outright: no documented positive catalyst means the Entry Checklist cannot be satisfied regardless of indicator alignment. Research only.

gappers.catalyst: Bounce after a brutal week (-17.2% in five sessions, -21.6% in a month) on renewed focus on Bloom's AI data-center power contracts, including a 702 MW project for Google's $17B Wyoming data center, against FY guidance raised a third time to $4.4-4.6B.
headlines: Google wants Bloom's fuel cells - Wall Street hates its cash burn (Investing.com, Nov 19)
Bloom Energy Named to TIME's 2027 Top Manufacturers List (Stock Titan, Nov 18)
'A Standard for AI Onsite Power': Bloom Energy Is Up 100% in 2026 - Is It Too Late to Buy? (TIKR, Nov 18)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Bloom is the only name on today's list where a strong company thesis and the macro bounce point the same way, but the proximate cause of the gap is recovery from a severe drawdown, not fresh news. Coverage dated Nov 19 recaps a 702 MW deployment for Google's $17B Wyoming data center among recent contracts, alongside Q3 results (revenue +138% y/y to $1.24B vs $1.06B expected, non-GAAP EPS $0.94 vs $0.69, operating margin 23.1% from 8.9%, first $1B+ product-revenue quarter) and FY26 guidance raised for the third time this year to $4.4-4.6B with non-GAAP EPS $3.10-3.40. The bear half is equally concrete: Q3 free cash flow -$181M, operating cash flow -$27M, capex $153M in the quarter and $231M YTD (~4x all of 2025), management explicitly guiding working capital to keep rising, and the stock at 98.9x trailing earnings. It fell 8.7% on earnings day and 17.2% last week.
gappers.why: Two mechanisms stack. Beta supplies the lift; underneath it, solid-oxide fuel cells supply on-site data-center power and bypass grid interconnection queues -- the actual bottleneck in AI capacity buildout -- so an NVDA beat reads through directly to power suppliers. The gap itself is a bounce: the stock lost 17.2% in a week, so this is dip-buying into a name whose guidance has gone up three times while the price went down.
gappers.impact: The most sustainable-looking move of the five, with the clearest caveat. 11.5M shares premarket is solid for a ~$50B cap, and the power complex corroborates with a real demand mechanism rather than pure correlation. But this is now the third bite at the same apple (Oct 22 print, Nov 12 NTT DATA 900 MW deal, today), and the thing that actually broke the stock last week -- negative free cash flow against a 98.9x multiple -- is untouched by a bounce. Note the dispersion in fair-value work: InvestingPro's model puts intrinsic value at $126.71, ~27% below spot, while the analyst median target is $283.85.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Three guidance raises plus contracted deployments (702 MW Google, 900 MW NTT DATA) are a structural reset, not a headline, and the AI-power theme aligns with the Technology/Industrials early-cycle row in TRADING-STRATEGY.md -- worth a multi-day/week swing hold if it clears Confluence on a later /trade check.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (flat book), so the cost is one weekly slot -- and on catalyst quality BE is the name worth spending it on, displacing ASTS, NBIS, CRWV and SATL (all beta-only or carrying a negative fundamental reset). It competes only with KLIC, which has a cleaner dated beat but less structural upside. Sizing is the binding constraint and the numbers do not agree: the 20% cap allows ~$20,000 (~108 shares at $184.00), while ATR(14) sizing at 1.0% risk allows just 46 shares -- and that figure is computed off a stale window (see the size.mjs defect note), so it must be recomputed before any order. R:R clears 2:1 at a sane stop: a 10% stop at ~$165.60 ($18.40 risk) needs ~$220.80, well inside the $351.28 52-week high and below the $283.85 median target. Research only; no size proposed.

headlines: Oppenheimer initiated coverage of Unusual Machines with an Outperform rating and $30 price target (TheFly, Nov 19)
Unusual Machines files registration statement for securities offering (Nov 13)
Piper Sandler lowers Unusual Machines price target to $27 from $29, keeps Overweight (Nov 9)
gappers.catalyst_detail: A dated, company-specific catalyst: Oppenheimer initiated UMAC at Outperform with a $30 target against a ~$9.61 prior close. That lands on a drone-components business that has grown fast and spent heavily. Q3 2026 (Nov 5) showed revenue ~$13.9M, up 551% y/y but down 17% sequentially, gross margin compressing to 35.4% from 39.4%, and a net loss of ~$25.0M ($0.50/share vs a 14c consensus loss) against ~$1.6M of net income a year earlier -- though $18.4M of that was an unrealized investment loss and $5.5M stock compensation. Cash was ~$162.0M at end-September and management targets positive adjusted EBITDA in 2027. The portfolio is unusual for a $499M-cap company: $30M equity in Powerus (PUSA), $27.5M in XTEND AI Robotics, $10M in Draganfly, plus the completed Upgrade Energy/DroneNX acquisition (Oct 19) and a $16.9M Powerus purchase order (Oct 22). The material offset is a registration statement filed Nov 13 for a securities offering.
gappers.why: A high-target initiation on a small ~$499M-cap, low-float-ish name is a direct demand shock: it supplies a price anchor roughly 3x spot, triggers momentum and short-covering buying, and is amplified by the risk-on tape. The mechanism is a sell-side anchor plus small-cap reflexivity, not an operating change -- nothing in the business changed between Nov 18 and Nov 19.
gappers.impact: Genuinely idiosyncratic, which separates UMAC from the rest of the list -- but on the shakiest foundation. 3.35M shares is light in absolute terms and the smallest premarket volume of the top five, so the move rests on a thinner book and can be unwound as easily as it was made. An initiation is an opinion, not a cash flow: the sequential revenue decline (-17%), compressing gross margin, and a 50c loss against a 14c consensus loss all point the other way, and the Nov 13 registration statement is a live supply overhang -- the single most common way a small-cap analyst-driven gap gets sold into. Note also the target dispersion: Oppenheimer $30, Northland Outperform, Piper Sandler $27 (cut from $29) -- all well above a $9.61 stock, which is itself a warning that sell-side targets here have not been predictive.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: An analyst initiation is a headline, not a structural change -- no new contract, guidance or regime shift -- and a pending securities offering caps upside; expect the anchor effect to fade within days.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Flat book, so nothing is displaced; the cost is one weekly slot spent on the smallest and least liquid name on the list. It is displaced by BE (structural, liquid) and arguably by KLIC (a hard earnings beat rather than an opinion). R:R mechanics are the cleanest-looking of the five and still do not justify it: a 10% stop at $9.27 ($1.03 risk) needs only ~$12.36 for 2:1, which is far inside the $27-30 analyst targets. The problem is stop integrity, not target distance -- $9.27 sits below yesterday's $9.61 close with no structure beneath it, in a name that just filed to sell stock, so a 10% trailing stop in a $1.60-ATR name is roughly 0.64 ATR and will be taken out by ordinary noise. ATR(14) sizing suggests 624 shares against a 1,680-share 20% cap, but both come from a stale price window and must be recomputed. Research only.

gappers.catalyst: Oversold neocloud bounce after a ~30% November slide; 2026 revenue outlook now narrowed to $3.0-3.2B (from $3.0-3.4B) and Nvidia's disclosed neocloud backing trimmed to $32B from $36B a quarter earlier.
headlines: Did Nvidia Earnings Just Shift Nebius Group's (NBIS) Investment Case? (Simply Wall St, Nov 19)
Nvidia Shrinks Neocloud Backing to $32 Billion as CoreWeave and Nebius Rallies Fade Fast (Barchart, Nov 18)
Nebius: Surging Capital Needs Amidst Tightening Liquidity (Seeking Alpha, Nov 18)
gappers.catalyst_detail: No positive company news is dated today; this is a bounce in a name that has been repriced downward all month. Q3 (Nov 12) grew revenue ~571% y/y, but the stock fell ~25% over the following two sessions on weak core revenue and soft guidance, and the 2026 outlook has since been narrowed to $3.0-3.2B -- the low end of the prior $3.0-3.4B range -- with ~40% adjusted EBITDA margin. Management will stop guiding to ARR after a February update. 2027 capex is guided at $40-45B against ~$27B in 2026, with 75-85% intended to come from customer prepayments and asset-backed financing rather than equity; a Nov 18 Seeking Alpha piece rates the shares Strong Sell on exactly that liquidity risk. Nvidia's reaffirmation of selective neocloud support came with its disclosed commitments shrinking to $32B from $36B.
gappers.why: Pure complex beta plus short covering off an oversold extreme, with the NVDA print as the excuse. The honest read is that the supposed bullish catalyst is a downgrade in disguise: the Nvidia backing number went down, not up, and the revenue range was narrowed to its low end. What the market has been repricing -- $40-45B of 2027 capex against tightening liquidity -- is untouched by a one-day bounce.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day spike likely to mean-revert, and the precedent is specific rather than theoretical. On Nov 18, on this identical driver, NBIS went +10.27% premarket and was +0.10% by 10:16 ET -- a complete round trip within 45 minutes of the open. Barchart's Nov 18 headline describes exactly that fade across both NBIS and IREN. 26.6M shares is heavy participation, but in a heavily shorted name that cuts both ways, and options flow skews defensive (58% of $168.7M premium in puts). CRWV at rank 5 on the same driver confirms this is complex-wide, not idiosyncratic.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The catalyst is market-wide, the company-specific news flow (narrowed guidance to the low end, ARR guidance being withdrawn, smaller Nvidia commitment) is negative, and the same setup round-tripped one session ago.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Flat book, so nothing is displaced; the cost is a weekly slot on the second attempt at a setup that failed 24 hours ago. Displaced by BE on catalyst quality, and it would itself likely block CRWV under the correlation gate (>0.75 with 2+ open positions -- run scripts/corr-gate.mjs before any entry, since NBIS and CRWV trade as one position in practice). R:R: at $113.89 a 10% stop sits at ~$102.50, which is inside the November range rather than below it, so 2:1 needs ~$136.67 -- above where the stock was before the Q3 print and requiring the market to re-accept guidance it has spent a month rejecting. The 2:1 gate is reachable on paper and implausible on thesis. Research only.

headlines: CoreWeave (CRWV): Assessing the Climb Toward $95 - no verified news or fundamental catalyst found (Tickeron, Nov 18)
Why Is CoreWeave Stock Falling? Nvidia Financing Fears (Stocks Down Under, Nov 18)
CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator Just Canceled His 10b5-1 Trading Plan (Barchart, Nov 17)
gappers.catalyst_detail: The highest-volume and lowest-information move on the list. Published analysis dated Nov 18 states plainly that no verified news or fundamental catalyst explains the stock's behaviour and that the move is technical, extending the post-Q3 unwind in a name averaging a 4.0% daily swing. The one discretionary signal is Nov 17: CEO Michael Intrator cancelled his 10b5-1 trading plan, which removes scheduled insider selling and is usually read as a confidence signal. Q3 (Nov 10) remains the frame: revenue +168% to $3.66B, backlog $132.5B (from $104.2B in Q2), 1.7 GW active and 4.6 GW contracted -- against a net loss of $709M after $846M of interest expense and total debt of $46.9B (from $35.6B). The stock lost ~32% in October on neocloud debt concerns, Bernstein cut its target to $51, and it traded near $48.11 on Nov 18.
gappers.why: The most leveraged expression of the AI-compute trade bouncing off an oversold extreme on a risk-on day -- short covering and mean reversion with no news attached. The backlog is genuinely structural, but what the market is repricing is $46.9B of debt and $846M of quarterly interest, and one session of risk-on resolves neither. The 10b5-1 cancellation is a signal about insider intent, not about cash flows.
gappers.impact: Most liquid and most volume-confirmed move on the list at 61.3M shares -- the highest of any qualifier -- but volume cuts both ways in a heavily shorted name, and the decisive evidence is price. Yesterday this exact name on this exact driver gapped ~4%, opened $51.07, and sold to $46.33 within 40 minutes. Today's $50.74 print is still below that failed open, so the stock has not yet reclaimed the level where it broke one session ago. NBIS at rank 4 on the identical driver marks the move as complex-wide. Read-through is sector-wide, not stock-specific.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The $132.5B backlog is structural, but the live risk ($46.9B debt, $846M quarterly interest) is unresolved, no catalyst is dated today, and the stock failed at almost exactly this price one session ago.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Flat book, so nothing is displaced. It would be blocked against NBIS by the correlation gate (same driver, same complex -- one slot, not two), and is displaced by BE on catalyst quality. It does have the best mechanical setup of the beta names: at $50.74 a 10% stop sits at ~$45.67, just under the $46.33 low that held yesterday and near the $40.58 52-week low, so there is real structure beneath the stop, and 2:1 needs ~$60.88. But that target sits above the failed $51.07 open and requires reclaiming the entire broken level, so the trade only pays 2:1 if today's gap holds where yesterday's did not. The genuine cost is a weekly slot on the second attempt at a 24-hour-old failed setup. Research only.
